title: Later labels: Emerson, Melrose Stompers, Vocalion and Richard M. Jones
summary: Allen runs through discography items. She recalls the 1939 Vocalion sides, Richard M. Jones as the connection to Melrose, and that she never recorded with Fletcher Henderson's band.

bands.name: Lizzie Miles and her Melrose Stompers
Lizzie Miles and her Creole Jazz Hounds

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I see here in the book you got Lizzie Miles and her Creole jazz hands on Emerson. Four O'clock Blues and Aggravating Papa. You remember anything about that record?

Yeah, but I wouldn't remember who the fellas were. Just like I tell you, you know, they just get any guy, you know, make up a combination like that, you see? So I wouldn't know who they were, who the fellas were. I wouldn't remember them, you know, who they were.
Lizzie Miles and her Melrose Stompers, you remember that bunch?
The Melrose Stompers, what piece was that?

They're for the Vecalion, that's all right, Daddy, and keep on knocking, number two. He's My Man, Mellow Rhythm, that was the instrumental only. Hold Me Parson, He's Red Hot to Me, 20 Grand Blues and Stranger Blues. You don't remember any of those?
No.
Cornette, saxophone, and rhythm.
No, I can't remember. I remember the record, making the record. I made that in, I think, 30, 39. Made that record in 39. Those records in 39.
I just picked up that. That's all right, Daddy, and keep on knocking, number two. I got that myself the other day.
Keep knocking, but you can't come in? Yeah. Yeah, and then Hold Me Parson, I Feel Religion coming on. You got that one?
No, I don't got that. I got to keep on knocking, number two.

And they got one, Hold Me Parson, I Feel Religion coming on, and an awful lot my man ain't got, but what he's got, he's got an awful lot, and what he's got, it sure ain't hard to me. That was a good one.
I see they got composers on this record I got. They got Wiggins, that would be James Wiggins, maybe, huh?
On which record?
On, I believe it's Keep On a Knocking.
Keep Knocking, but you can't come in?
Yeah.
Well, Melrose said that was his, I don't know. Oh, yeah.
What about Big Bill? Did you ever know Big Bill Brooms? Was he on any of his?
No. Miney Jones is the one that got that connection for me with Melrose. Miney Jones, who wrote Caledonia?
Oh, yeah.
Miney Jones. Trouble in Miney. Yeah, yeah, that's right.
Richard M. Jones.
Richard M. Jones, we call him Miney. Yeah, that's right, that's right. Well, that Keep Knocking, that was just the same like the bucket got a hole in it. Yeah, that was the one.
Oh, yeah.
Mm-hmm.
Do you remember I was making any records with Fletcher Anderson?

No, I never made records with Fletcher Anderson. Mm-hmm. The only band that I made records was when I went for the OK, wait for the OK was this white band that was the studio band, then King Oliver and his group. Well, this little, that was a little small combination on the, with that vocabula, keep knocking but you can't come in. That was, I think it was about four, huh? Three or four of them. Yeah, that's all. That's all. Most all of my records was piano. You know, most piano records. Mm-hmm.
